issues.description: The non-overlap invariant ignores the nodes already write-locked by a `Locking` cursor, so it cannot establish exclusive ownership when that cursor becomes `Locked`.
issues.rationale: `inv_non_overlapping` constrains only pairs of cursors that are already in `Locked`; it says nothing about a `Locking(rt, nid)` cursor even though the protocol has already changed every traversed node in `[rt, nid)` from `Free` to `Locked`. Consequently, the pre-state of `protocol_lock_end` may satisfy the invariant while another CPU owns an overlapping `Locked` subtree, and the transition then creates two overlapping `Locked` cursors. The preservation proof exposes exactly this missing fact: both cases in which the completing CPU is one of the compared cursors end in `admit()`. The author first reported that a stronger invariant tracking different cursor states was needed, and the human reviewer then independently clarified that RCU `Locking(nid1, nid2)` represents write ownership of `[nid1, nid2)` and requested a change to `inv_non_overlapping`. This issue remains in the fixed final source.
issues.verification: source-only; historical Verus was not executed. Independently inspected the final invariant, lock transitions, and inductive preservation proof. The missing Locking-vs-Locked ownership relation admits an overlapping-cursor pre-state, and both affected proof branches remain explicitly admitted in the final head.
